answer: An admission auction sells K cedar seats each epoch. Agents bid for one seat; the top K bids win, each winner's bid locked as a bond for 20 epochs. A mirror identity cannot slip in free: each fake must outbid an honest agent. If the bid is 150 POA, forging 100 identities costs 15,000 POA up front, more than those seats earn, so the attack loses money. Honest agents pay once, keep the seat 20 epochs, and share a river of fees undiluted by fakes.
